posts.title: History leakage: The product explaining its own edit history
posts.description: Ask an agent to change a scoring model in your dashboard and you’ll find “New score: 50 (was 35)”. Ask it to rename a function and you get scoreV2 sitting next to the legacy_weights it didn’t dare to delete. Ask for a docs edit and the page says “now supports Parquet”. posts.title: They all write, store and read data: how to pick the right database
posts.description: A database in essence does three things: write, store and read data. A text file can do the same thing, so why do we need 20 different types of databases? Graph, document, vector, OLAP, OLTP, real-time, they all serve a purpose once you reach a certain scale and your requirements change. posts.title: Querying the entire internet with DuckDB and Common Crawl
posts.description: DuckDB is small. The data it queries doesn’t have to be. So let’s try something big. Common Crawl has been crawling and publishing web pages since 2008, and every crawl lands on S3 for anyone to read. Coding agents have turned a lot of people into web developers, so here is the internet-sized question for today: how much has personal, platform-hosted publishing actually grown?
